stem: A client asks what federal mental health parity protections generally mean when a health plan provides both medical/surgical benefits and mental health or substance use disorder benefits. Which response by the nurse is accurate?

options.A: The plan must cover every possible mental health and substance use disorder service without utilization limits
options.B: Financial requirements and treatment limitations for mental health or substance use disorder benefits generally cannot be more restrictive than the applicable parity standard for medical/surgical benefits
options.C: Parity requires every health plan in the United States to add mental health and substance use disorder benefits even if the plan otherwise would not provide them
options.D: Parity means mental health benefits must use exactly the same clinicians and facilities as medical/surgical benefits

rationale: CMS explains that MHPAEA generally prevents plans and issuers that provide both medical/surgical and mental health or substance use disorder benefits from imposing financial requirements or treatment limitations on MH/SUD benefits that are more restrictive than the predominant requirements or limitations applying to substantially all medical/surgical benefits in the relevant classification. Therefore B is the best answer. MHPAEA itself does not require every plan to offer MH/SUD benefits, does not prohibit all utilization limits, and does not require the same clinicians or facilities for both benefit types.
educational_objective: Explain the core MHPAEA parity protection without incorrectly stating that the law itself requires every plan to offer mental health or substance use disorder coverage.
source_document_title: The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA)
source_locator: Introduction; 2013 MHPAEA Regulations — financial requirements and treatment limitations cannot be more restrictive than the predominant requirements/limitations applying to substantially all medical/surgical benefits; MHPAEA does not require plans to provide MH/SUD benefits
source_claim_supported: When a plan provides both medical/surgical and MH/SUD benefits, MHPAEA generally requires parity in financial requirements and treatment limitations; MHPAEA itself does not require every plan to offer MH/SUD benefits.

correction_summary: Replaced the overbroad statement that parity laws universally require comparable insurance coverage with the exact MHPAEA rule. Explicitly preserved the statutory limitation that MHPAEA itself does not require every plan to offer MH/SUD benefits. Corrected blueprint from Health Promotion and Maintenance to Management of Care — Client Rights/Advocacy and replaced weak distractors with legally plausible but incorrect alternatives.
audit_findings: B matches current CMS guidance. A incorrectly converts parity into unlimited coverage. C incorrectly states that MHPAEA itself mandates MH/SUD coverage in every plan. D invents a same-provider/facility requirement. The stem identifies the condition under which the parity comparison applies, eliminating scope ambiguity. No second defensible answer, cueing, unsupported numerical precision, or unresolved legal conflict remains.
